supplements.citation: GIS 25DC059; 07-ADM-09; 18 NYCRR §387.9 — NY resource rules (eliminated under categorical eligibility)
supplements.heading: New York: NO asset test for categorically eligible households (most applicants)
supplements.text: New York eliminated the SNAP resource test for categorically eligible households effective January 1, 2008 (07-ADM-09): 'Most households applying for SNAP no longer have to pass a savings/resource test in order to get SNAP benefits. This means that the household's assets (stocks, savings and retirement accounts, etc.) are not considered when determining eligibility' (otda.ny.gov/programs/snap). Because nearly every NY household reaches SNAP through a categorical-eligibility pathway (see the income-pathways rule), asking an applicant about savings or vehicles is usually the WRONG move — 07-ADM-09 told districts that 'Workers will no longer need to verify resource information for almost all income-eligible households.' The resource test survives ONLY for households that are NOT categorically eligible — chiefly households containing a member sanctioned or disqualified for an Intentional Program Violation, work-rules failure, voluntary job quit, or failure to comply with periodic reporting (18 NYCRR §387.14(a)(5)(ii)), and aged/disabled households over 200% FPL taking the federal net-income-only path. (An ABAWD who merely timed out is NOT 'sanctioned' for this purpose — 16-ADM-06.) For those households the FFY 2026 limits are '$3,000' for standard households and '$4,500' for aged/disabled households — 'A resource test only applies in situations where the household is not categorically eligible' (GIS 25DC059, eff. 10/1/2025). STALENESS TRAP: the regulation text at 18 NYCRR §387.9 still prints the old $2,000/$3,000 figures (and its $3,000 tier reads 'age 60 or over' only, without the disabled-member arm) — the annual GIS controls the dollar values, not the regulation.

supplements.citation: GIS 25DC059; 07-ADM-09; 09-ADM-06; 16-ADM-06; 18 NYCRR §387.14 — NY income pathways (three simultaneous BBCE tiers)
supplements.heading: New York runs THREE simultaneous BBCE income tiers — 200% / 150% / 130% — there is no single income limit
supplements.text: New York is the state that kills any scalar income limit: three broad-based categorical eligibility gross-income tiers run simultaneously, on top of plain categorical eligibility for households where all members get Temporary Assistance or SSI. (1) 200% FPL — 'SNAP households containing any aged or disabled members, and households that pay out-of-pocket dependent care costs, that pass the 200% FPL gross income test and do not contain a SNAP-sanctioned or an Intentional Program Violation (IPV) member are categorically eligible for SNAP, meaning they are not subject to a resource test' (GIS 25DC059). (2) 150% FPL — 'SNAP households with earned income that do not contain a household member that is sanctioned or disqualified for an IPV, failure to comply with work rules or voluntary job quit, that do not contain an aged or disabled member, and that do not pay out-of-pocket dependent care costs, must pass the 150% FPL gross income test' (GIS 25DC059; established by 16-ADM-06, eff. 7/1/2016). (3) 130% FPL for everyone else (07-ADM-09, eff. 1/1/2008, the original BBCE directive via the TANF-funded 'Helping Hands' vehicle). FFY 2026 monthly values (eff. 10/1/2025) for a household of 1: 200% = $2,608; 150% = $1,957; 130% = $1,696; 100% net = $1,305. Household of 4: $5,358 / $4,019 / $3,483 / $2,680. TRAP: there is NO 165% eligibility tier in NY — the 165% FPL figure in the standards table is only the elderly-disabled SEPARATE-HOUSEHOLD (purchase-and-prepare) rule: an elderly person unable to buy/prepare food separately may apply as their own food unit if the OTHERS' income is at or below 165% FPL. (The Source Book's §11 five-test list does include a '165% GIT' — that test gates separate-food-unit status against the others' income, never a household's own eligibility.) Aged/disabled households OVER 200% lose categorical eligibility but can still qualify under the federal net-only rule (100% net test + $4,500 resource test). Households with a sanctioned/IPV member can never be categorically eligible; they face 130% gross + 100% net + resource tests — UNLESS the household contains an aged/disabled member, in which case only the 100% net test + resource test apply, and a sanctioned household paying dependent care gets a 150% gross test (SNAP Source Book §11.1). Directive lineage: 07-ADM-09 (130% general + aged/disabled 200%), 09-ADM-06 (dependent-care to 200%), 16-ADM-06 (earned-income to 150%) — codified at 18 NYCRR §387.14. (12-ADM-06 is a Flexible Fund directive, NOT the BBCE authority — a known miscitation.) The 'Helping Hands' text is no longer a separately mailed brochure; it is embedded in client approval notices (SNAP Source Book §5, citing 12-INF-12).

supplements.citation: GIS 25DC059; GIS 25DC061; SNAP Source Book §12 — NY utility allowances (REGIONAL three-tier SUAs)
supplements.heading: New York SUAs are REGIONAL — NYC $1,062 / Nassau-Suffolk $988 / Rest of State $877 — and OBBBA rewired the HEAP shortcut
supplements.text: New York's utility allowances vary by REGION — never quote one statewide number. FFY 2026 values (GIS 25DC059, eff. 10/1/2025): Heating/Air-Conditioning SUA ('HT/AC') — NYC $1,062, Nassau & Suffolk $988, Rest of State $877; Utility SUA ('UTIL') — NYC $419, Nassau & Suffolk $388, Rest of State $355; Phone SUA — $32 everywhere. The HT/AC and Utility amounts include 'water, sewage, and trash collection.' VOCABULARY TRAP: NYC's ABEL budgeting system uses different names — the HT/AC SUA is the 'Combined Heat/Utility/Phone SUA' and the Utility SUA is the 'Limited Utility Allowance' ('LUA') in NYC ABEL (GIS 25DC059). OBBBA REWIRING (GIS 25DC061, retroactive to July 4, 2025): receipt of a qualifying HEAP/LIHEAP payment 'only confers HCSUA eligibility to households containing an aged and/or disabled member. All other households must establish that they have a separate heating or cooling utility expense.' Districts 'must not use LIHEAP receipt as a basis for granting the HCSUA unless the household has at least one member who qualifies as Aged or Disabled.' Households that lose the heating SUA 'may instead be entitled to the Utility SUA if they have a separate expense for a non-heating/cooling utility... electricity, cooking fuel, sewage, trash collection, water fees, fuel for heating hot water, and rental fee for a propane tank' — and 'Most households do, at a minimum, incur some expense for telephone use and are therefore eligible for at least the Telephone SUA.' Districts must not strip the HCSUA mid-certification based solely on the household lacking an aged/disabled member — the change applies at the next determination, and the GIS says districts 'should confirm' whether a separate cooling expense exists before removing it. To establish a cooling expense: a verified electricity bill plus the household's attestation that part of it pays for cooling is sufficient — the cooling portion itself need not be separately verified (GIS 25DC061). NYC's implementation (per HRA): November 1, 2025 for new and pending applications, with existing households assessed at recertification or periodic report — against the state's retroactive-to-7/4/25 framing.

supplements.citation: SNAP Source Book §12/§13 (Sept 2025); GIS 25DC059 — NY deductions (child support is an EXCLUSION; no standard medical)
supplements.heading: New York deductions — child support is an income EXCLUSION, there is NO standard medical deduction, dependent care is uncapped
supplements.text: Three NY-specific facts control deduction math. (1) CHILD SUPPORT IS AN EXCLUSION, NOT A DEDUCTION: 'Both legally obligated and informal child support payments (current and arrears) made by a SNAP household member to non-household members shall be treated as income exclusions' — ABEL 'will subtract the child support payments from total household gross monthly income before comparing income to the applicable gross and net income limits' (emphasis: this runs BEFORE the gross tests), and 'Child support payments are excluded when screening for Expedited Processing' (SNAP Source Book §13.G.2). The exclusion is disallowed when the support payee lives in the same SNAP household as the payer. That means paying child support can move a household UNDER a gross-income tier — it is not merely a net-income deduction. (2) NO STANDARD MEDICAL DEDUCTION: unlike states running an SMD, New York offers only actual unreimbursed medical expenses over $35/month for households with an elderly or disabled member: 'Any household that has at least one member who is elderly or disabled... is eligible for a deduction of medical expenses in excess of $35 per month (per household) which are not reimbursed...' — estimates are allowed, and the amount is not reduced between recertifications. (3) DEPENDENT CARE IS UNCAPPED: 'The Dependent Care deduction is uncapped. The full out-of-pocket amount paid for Dependent Care is the actual amount to be included as a deduction' — and paying ANY out-of-pocket dependent care also moves the household to the 200% gross tier. Earned-income deduction: 'twenty percent of gross earnings' (SNAP Source Book §12.C). Dollar values as NY states them (GIS 25DC059, eff. 10/1/2025): standard deduction $209 (HH 1–3) / $223 (4) / $261 (5) / $299 (6+); excess-shelter cap $744 (shelter over 50% of adjusted income, UNCAPPED for elderly/disabled households); homeless shelter deduction $198.99 (the household 'must incur or anticipate incurring an expense, no matter how small') — with a twist: 'Actual expenses must be used as the shelter deduction for homeless households which verify incurred expenses which exceed the standard deduction.' Boarder/lodger exclusion: $298 (1) / $546 (2).

supplements.citation: 25-ADM-03; GIS 26DC012; 26-INF-03; 18 NYCRR §385.3 — NY ABAWD rules (fixed statewide clock)
supplements.heading: New York ABAWD — FIXED statewide 36-month window (Oct 1, 2023 – Sep 30, 2026), in effect statewide since March 1, 2026
supplements.text: New York runs a FIXED statewide ABAWD clock: 'the 36-month period has the same beginning and end date in all districts for all ABAWDs. The current fixed 36-month period began on October 1, 2023, and will expire on September 30, 2026. A new 36-month period will begin on October 1, 2026' (25-ADM-03-P) — everyone's countable months reset together (unlike Texas's per-person rolling clock). POST-OBBBA: an ABAWD is 'aged 18 to 64' with a time limit of three countable months per period; 'The exemptions from the ABAWD time limit for individuals experiencing homelessness, veterans, and youth aging out of foster care were removed with the passage of H.R. 1.' Current exceptions include: under 18 or 65+; pregnant; 'residing in a SNAP household with a child under the age of 14'; 'Indians, Urban Indians, and California Indians as such terms are defined in the Indian Health Care Improvement Act'; medically unfit (receipt of public or private disability benefits, unable to work 80 hours/month for physical/mental reasons, or obviously unfit — interpreted broadly per 26-ADM-02); plus the general-work-rules exemptions (working 30+ hrs/week or earning $217.50+/week, student half-time, caring for a child under 6 or an incapacitated person, unemployment applicant/recipient, treatment program, SSI, TANF work rules). Exemptions may be self-attested unless questionable. WAIVER WHIPLASH — cite carefully by date: FNS terminated NY's waiver effective 11/2/2025 (25-ADM-03-P); litigation reinstated it through 2/28/2026 for every county EXCEPT Saratoga, which was never in the state's waiver (GIS 25DC081; 25-ADM-03-P); and the CURRENT status (GIS 26DC012) is that the time limit operates in ALL districts since March 1, 2026, with ONLY the Tuscarora Nation Reservation and Poospatuck (State) Reservation waived March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027. New York City is NOT waived — HRA implemented the rules November 1, 2025, with compliance required beginning March 1, 2026 (NYC HRA). November 2025 is not a countable month anywhere (federal-shutdown FNS memo, GIS 25DC089); countable-month tracking began March 2026 in all districts EXCEPT Saratoga County, where it began December 1, 2025. Meeting the rules: 80 hours/month of work (paid, in-kind, or 20 hrs/week), approved training, or community service — community-service hours are the SNAP benefit DIVIDED by the higher of the federal or State minimum wage, rounded down to the whole hour (e.g. $300 ÷ $16.00 = 18 hours/month). Earning $217.50/week or more exempts outright. Hours dropping below 80/month must be reported within 10 days after the end of the month. Regaining: verify prospective compliance at application, or complete 80 hours in ANY consecutive 30-day period; after regaining then losing compliance again, the INDIVIDUAL gets ONE extra set of three CONSECUTIVE months per 36-month period (once issued, all three run even if the person becomes exempt). The district must offer help regaining. DISTINCT MECHANISM: failing the GENERAL work rules triggers the Conciliation Notification process and a 1/3/6-month sanction ladder — that is not the ABAWD time limit; an LDSS-5127 appointment no-show is not sanctionable.

supplements.citation: SNAP Source Book §6/§14 (Sept 2025); 18 NYCRR §387.17 — NY certification periods + reporting + interviews
supplements.heading: New York certs + reporting — 24-month cap, LDSS-4310 periodic report, telephone-default interviews
supplements.text: Certification periods 'conform to calendar months and begin with the month of application' and 'are not to exceed twenty-four months, except for households that participate in the NYS Combined Application Project (NYSCAP) or Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP)' (SNAP Source Book). All-elderly/disabled households with very stable income get up to 24 months (18 NYCRR §387.17); most other households run on simplified (six-month) reporting cycles. REPORTING: simplified reporting is the NY default. Households certified seven FULL months or longer must return the WMS-generated Periodic Report (LDSS-4310) 'by the tenth day of the sixth month of their certification period' — failure closes the case (reason E50), curable via LDSS-4310A. For non-ABAWD simplified reporters the ONLY mandatory mid-certification report is the 130% trigger (an ABAWD must additionally report work hours falling below 80/month — even during TBA): 'If the household's gross monthly income exceeds the 130% of the poverty level, it must be reported... within 10 days following the month of change' — and this applies 'even if it is subject to a higher SNAP gross income limit due to broad-based categorical eligibility or the presence of an aged or disabled household member.' Other changes (earned income shifts of more than $125, household composition, address/rent, child-support order changes) are reported at the three contact points: application, Periodic Report, recertification. INTERVIEWS: New York holds a standing federal State-Plan approval 'to conduct telephone interviews in lieu of face-to-face interviews for SNAP, without documenting hardship at initial application or recertification. Households maintain the right to a face-to-face interview upon request.' An interview IS still required — the pandemic-era skip-interview waiver 'permanently expire[d] on October 31, 2024' (GIS 24DC028). Missed interview → LDSS-4753 'SNAP Request For Contact/Missed Interview' notice, and 'no SNAP application is denied prior to the 30th day from the application date for failure to appear.' RECERTIFICATION: packet mails ~2 months before the period ends; submit the recert application (myBenefits.ny.gov, mail, fax, or in person), then interview (telephone default), then documents; timely filing protects uninterrupted benefits. TBA: when a Temporary Assistance case closes, otherwise-qualified households get Transitional Benefits Alternative SNAP — a FIXED five months at the frozen amount with no reporting during the period except an ABAWD's hours-below-80 report, then recertification (09-ADM-22). IN NYC (per HRA): interviews are ON-DEMAND — 'You must call HRA to complete your interview at the number you were provided... HRA will not call you' (On Demand line 929-273-1872); an in-center, including face-to-face, interview at a SNAP Center remains a right.

supplements.citation: SNAP Source Book §4/§14; GIS 21DC079; 24-ADM-09; 18 NYCRR §387.8 — ESAP, NYSCAP, and expedited processing
supplements.heading: New York simplified tracks — ESAP 36-month certs with waived recert interview, NYSCAP auto-enrollment for SSI singles, 7-day expedited
supplements.text: New York runs three burden-reduction tracks. ESAP (Elderly Simplified Application Project, since 2021 — GIS 21 TA/DC079): for households where 'all adult members are seniors (age 60 or older) and/or disabled and are not otherwise eligible to participate in... NYSCAP' and 'no household members have any earned income.' ESAP certs run up to 36 months, the application is the two-page LDSS-5166, shelter/utility costs may be self-declared unless questionable (electronic matches verify income/SSN/DOB), the mid-point interim report (LDSS-3151, the 'SNAP Change Report Form') is NON-mandatory, and at renewal 'a recertification interview is not required but may be requested' — the initial-application interview still applies and expedited processing is unchanged. NYSCAP (NYS Combined Application Project — replaced NYSNIP as of November 30, 2024, per 24-ADM-09): for SSI recipients in single-person households; it 'automatically opens SNAP cases at an amount no less than the minimum monthly SNAP benefit' (the federal minimum is $24 for FFY 2026 per GIS 25DC059; 24-ADM-09's '$23' is the pre-COLA figure), with 36-month certification, a MANDATORY interim contact at month 18 (LDSS-4836), and a 90-day benefit-redemption rule. EXPEDITED: New York's issuance standard is SEVEN calendar days — 'SNAP benefits must be made available to eligible households no later than seven calendar days following the day the application was filed' (Source Book; 18 NYCRR §387.8). Criteria: gross income under $150 AND liquid resources at or below $100 in the application month; OR destitute migrant/seasonal farmworker with liquid resources ≤ $100; OR combined gross income and liquid resources LESS than the month's shelter costs. Screening is same-day on the mandatory LDSS-3938; only IDENTITY must be verified before expedited issuance; there is no limit on how many times a household can use expedited, provided previously postponed verification was resolved. STALE-TEXT TRAP: one Source Book line still prints a '5 days' expedited figure (citing §387.5) — the operative standard everywhere else in the Source Book, the regulation, and the public FAQ is seven calendar days. IN NYC (per HRA): E-SNAP provides a one-time issuance within 5 calendar days for eligible expedited cases — an HRA statement (the same HRA FAQ elsewhere says 7 calendar days; HRA's page is internally inconsistent), not the state standard.

supplements.citation: New York SNAP — OTDA, 58 local districts (18 NYCRR Part 387; myBenefits statewide / ACCESS HRA in NYC)
supplements.heading: New York program identity — OTDA supervises, 58 districts administer, and NYC runs on a DIFFERENT portal
supplements.text: New York uses the plain federal name 'SNAP' — no state branding. Structure: OTDA (Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance) supervises; '58 local social services districts, which include each county and New York City,' administer directly (state-supervised, county-administered). New York City's district is HRA (Human Resources Administration, part of NYC DSS — the largest local social services agency in the country). TWO-PORTAL REALITY: outside NYC, apply, recertify, track, report changes, and upload documents at myBenefits.ny.gov (a SNAP guest account works for applying). IN NYC, the portal is ACCESS HRA (nyc.gov/accesshra, web + mobile app with document upload and appointment tracking) — 'Apply online using ACCESS HRA. You can apply for Cash Assistance, SNAP, and Medicaid all at the same time' — and myBenefits does not appear on NYC's SNAP pages. The paper form works statewide: LDSS-4826 'SNAP Application/Recertification' (Rev. 12/23, 12 pages, SNAP-only — the multi-program common application is a different form); the authorized-representative form is LDSS-4942. Applications can be filed online, by mail, by fax, or in person — at the local district office, or in NYC at a SNAP Center in any borough; eligible households must receive benefits 'no later than 30 days from the date the local district received your application.' Applicant rights (as HRA states them): an office must accept a signed application with a readable name, and interviews can be done by phone. Policy lives in the SNAP Source Book (Sept 2025 edition) and issues via OTDA's directive system — ADM (Administrative Directive), INF (Informational Letter), LCM (Local Commissioners Memorandum), and GIS (General Information System) messages — with final authority in 18 NYCRR Part 387. Contacts: OTDA SNAP hotline 1-800-342-3009; fair hearings 1-800-342-3334 (online request form available; NYC emergency fair hearings 800-205-0110); NYC HRA On Demand interview line 929-273-1872 and 718-SNAP-Now for recertification interviews. EBT: benefits ride the Common Benefit Identification Card (CBIC); balance and card-freeze via ebtEDGE (photos/signatures removed from new and replacement cards for Temporary Assistance recipients effective December 1, 2024).

supersessions.273.24: NEW YORK: fixed statewide 36-month clock (current window Oct 1, 2023 – Sep 30, 2026; next begins Oct 1, 2026, per 25-ADM-03). Time limit operates in ALL districts since March 1, 2026 (GIS 26DC012); only the Tuscarora and Poospatuck reservations are waived through Feb 28, 2027. November 2025 is not countable (GIS 25DC089); countable-month tracking began March 2026 except Saratoga County (December 1, 2025 — never in the state's waiver).
supersessions.273.9: NEW YORK: the OBBBA (H.R. 1) heat-and-eat restriction (federal overlay §10103) is implemented by GIS 25DC061, retroactive to July 4, 2025 — HEAP/LIHEAP receipt confers the heating SUA only for households with an aged/disabled member; all others must show an actual heating/cooling expense (fallback: Utility SUA, then Phone SUA).
